Subject: Post-demo: Benchmark pack, Redwood-verified profiles & SLA checklist

Hi Emily / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo + the next steps to get a short pilot running: 

TL;DR
- We recorded Redwood-verified benchmark profiles for the recommended candidate models and shared a lightweight benchmark pack (links below).
- Suggested pilot: 2-week functional & perf run with 50k monthly tokens, can run on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated pool depending on your isolation needs.
- Action items: BrightLane to share 3 representative prompt sets and a small sample dataset; Redwood to provision pilot env and provide runbook + SLA checklist.

What we saw (summary of the demo traces)
- Candidate model shortlist: rdw-7b-q4f (fast, quantized), rdw-13b-8k (balanced throughput + quality), llama2-70b-instruct (highest quality; higher cost).
- Redwood-verified perf snapshot (typical short instruction workload, 32-token generations):
  * rdw-7b-q4f — throughput: 280 TPS (batching enabled), p50 latency: 18 ms, p95 latency: 60 ms
  * rdw-13b-8k — throughput: 120 TPS, p50 latency: 42 ms, p95 latency: 140 ms
  * llama2-70b-instruct — throughput: 22 TPS, p50 latency: 220 ms, p95 latency: 380 ms

Quality notes and regression risks
- For summary / triage workloads you highlighted, rdw-13b-8k is our recommended sweet spot. It balances accuracy with predictable latency.
- Key regression risks we flagged: prompt sensitivity around system tokens (we observed ~6% ROUGE drop with a prompt prefix change in a small sample) and tokenization differences for medical shorthand. We recommend:
  1) A short prompt normalization pass (we can provide a template).
  2) A 1,000-example regression eval run prior to any rollout to detect drift.

Attachments and links
- Attached: pilot MOP (brightlane_pilot_mop.pdf) and the raw benchmark workbook (redwood_benchmarks_2028_q2.xlsx).
- Shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/brightlane/benchmarks/2028-08-29
- Model profile quicklinks: https://console.redwood.ai/models/rdw-13b-8k/profile (includes per-sequence TPS and latency CDFs)

Next steps (owner/ETA)
1) BrightLane: share 3 prompt sets + 500-record sample dataset — owner: Emily — due: 2028-09-05
2) Redwood: provision pilot env, upload pilot runbook and SLA checklist — owner: Kimberly — due: 2028-09-01
3) Joint: schedule pilot kickoff (30m) — tentative week of 2028-09-11 — owner: Ben to coordinate calendars

If that aligns, I’ll kick off the HubSpot record and drop the pilot links in a follow-up email.

Thanks —

Emily —

Great question. Short answer: the numbers I shared are from steady-state runs with warmed instances (no cold-starts). For p99/cold-start scenarios we observed (rdw-13b-8k):
  * cold-start p99: ~1.1s (instances starting from idle),
  * warmed p99: ~260 ms with our continuous batching configuration.

Notes and mitigation options we recommend:
- Provision a small warmed pool (reserved capacity) for the pilot windows where you expect spikes — that reduces cold-start p99 to warmed p99.
- Use the prefix/KV caching hooks for repeated patient-context calls — can reduce per-request latency by 30–50% depending on prompt reuse.
- For EHR batch uploads we suggest: async batch job pattern (queue + streaming inference) vs. synchronous, to keep user-facing SLOs tight.

I attached a short SLA checklist in the pilot MOP that lists recommended reserved capacity sizing and a fallback plan (model variant fallback to rdw-7b-q4f for non-critical requests).

If you want, Ben can run a quick traffic-profile sizing session tomorrow to estimate reserved capacity cost for a 24/7 pilot window.

—Kimberly

Hi Emily —

I can run a short capacity-sizing run tomorrow. Two quick asks before we size: 
1) Can you share a 48-hour traffic histogram (or even a representative hour) so I can model batching behavior?
2) Which requests are user-facing vs. back-office (batch) so we can map the right SLOs to each flow?

We’ll sketch two options in the runbook:
- Option A (cost-conscious): Hosted with autoscaling + KV caching, fallback to rdw-7b-q4f for bulk batch jobs. Expected pilot cost: ~$4,200 over 2 weeks (ballpark).
- Option B (SLA-focused): Dedicated reserved pool with a warmed baseline. Expected pilot cost: ~$11,500 over 2 weeks (ballpark) — includes reserved capacity for p99 targets.

I’ll drop draft costed options into the HubSpot deal after the histogram — should be quick.
